# Challenges about peer review

- Editorial decisions often rely on subjective interpretation of reviewer comments.
- Verifying whether a reviewer comment is supported by the manuscript is time-consuming.
- Different editors may reach different conclusions on the same comment.
- Important evidence can be overlooked when papers are long and complex.
- Assessing hundreds of reviewer comments creates a significant workload.
- Limited transparency makes it difficult to justify editorial decisions.
- Inconsistent evaluations can lead to unfair treatment of authors.
- Manual review processes are difficult to scale as submission volumes increase.

## Advantages of Our Work for Peer Review

- Supports editors by linking reviewer comments to paper evidence.
- Makes peer review decisions more transparent and explainable.
- Reduces manual effort in checking whether comments are supported.
- Combines RAG retrieval with model-based evidence evaluation.
- Provides confidence scores to help prioritize difficult cases.
- Keeps the human editor as the final decision-maker.
- Helps identify unsupported, partially supported, or unclear reviewer comments.

## Importance of Grid5000 in Our Work

- Provided a reliable research infrastructure for running our experiments.
- Offered a private computing environment for processing papers and reviews.
- Supported GPU-based execution of large language models.
- Enabled scalable experiments beyond local machine capacity.
- Available in Europe, including Western Europe, which supported our research context.
- Helped ensure more controlled and reproducible model testing.
- Served as the main infrastructure for our Evidence-RAG pipeline.
:::

## Future Steps

- Test the system with more papers and reviewer comments.
- Compare results across different models and retrieval settings.
- Improve the confidence score with editor feedback.
- Add more human editors to evaluate fairness and consistency.
- Build a clearer dashboard for reviewing evidence and decisions.
- Study how Evidence-RAG can reduce workload in real editorial workflows.
- Extend the system to support more journals and disciplines.
